description: Recipient-side evaluation, acceptance steps 7-11 (spec 6.7). The recipient's org policy is world.org_policies['example.org']; the recipient's delegates are in world.delegates. An agent may receive a message only if no kill switch blocks it and the policy's clients list allows its client; with to.delegate, only the agent it names counts. state.recent is the count of messages already accepted in the grant's rate-limit window. Thread checks (step 8's participants, state and replies) and the semantic rules that compare a message with others in its thread are out of scope here: an envelope that names in_reply_to answers a request the recipient sent in an open thread of the envelope's scope, which the recipient's broker holds under that in_reply_to_hash.

cases.name: accepted through the default relationship and delivered
a decline is accepted without field coverage (common-type body)
stranger's message is refused and becomes a contact attempt
field outside the recipient's receive list
note refused: the recipient narrowed the default and left /note out
inbound classification rule (financial figure from outside)
a rule that lists only restricted.* also matches the label restricted itself (spec 6.5)
inbound DLP on free text
delivery constraint no delegate meets: held for the person's web view
rate limit of the relationship
body fails the scope schema at the recipient
quiet hours: accepted and held
a grant bound to an earlier holder of the sender's address is void: a contact attempt (spec 5.2)
a retention constraint the broker can't honor
to.delegate names one of the recipient's agents that may receive it: delivered
to.delegate names no agent of the recipient's: accepted and held for the person, never refused and never given to the person's other agents (spec 6.7)
to.delegate names an agent the organization blocked: held for the person (spec 5.8, 6.7)
to.delegate names an agent whose client the organization's list doesn't name: held for the person (spec 6.7, 6.10)
to.delegate names an agent that doesn't meet the delivery constraints, though another of the recipient's agents does: held for the person (spec 6.7, 6.11)
a reply asking a further question, from the analyst, is accepted like a first request, and delivered
a question back (a request answering a request) from the leader is refused at the analyst's broker: the default's reverse terms have no request
an ack needs no may: accepted though the recipient's narrowed grant allows only requests
